extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from primary activity result, docking/SMD/MD sections, Figure 3-6 captions, and Supplementary Table S2. Computational binding claims are not promoted to direct cellular antiviral mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: BRIP directly inhibits SARS-CoV-2 Mpro enzymatic activity in vitro, with source-reported IC50 of 0.52 nM.

source_locator.method_locator: xml:sec=17:In vitro inhibition assay of Mpro

mechanism_claims.limitations: The assay supports target-enzyme inhibition, not whole-virus replication inhibition or clinical efficacy.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Docking and steered MD identify Mpro binding pocket 2 as the strongest modeled BRIP binding site, with Gln189 H-bond context and additional non-bonded contacts.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=6:Modeling of BRIP and detection of Mpro binding site

mechanism_claims.limitations: Docking/SMD evidence supports a proposed binding mode only; it is not independent direct mechanism proof in cells.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Conventional MD and MM-PBSA analyses support a stable modeled Mpro-BRIP complex with favorable van der Waals and electrostatic binding-energy contributions.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=9:Mpro and BRIP formed a stable protein-peptide complex

mechanism_claims.limitations: Computational complex stability is mechanism context only and is bounded below direct antiviral or cellular mechanistic evidence.
